title: Prove actual multitape parking/restoration and canonical-output conversion
body:
The existing finite multitape toolkit now includes a concrete fixed controller and charged output conversion. This extends PR1641 with actual all-length execution proofs; selected supplier profiles and kappa remain unchanged.

The five-tape, four-symbol, 90-state controller pushes the inactive stream, transfers the active stream, executes a real bit-flip child, transfers its output back and pops the inactive stream. For every active list x, inactive list y, absolute parking head and arbitrary ancestor cell function, `ParkingController.boundary_machine_correct` proves an actual run in exactly **6|x|+5|y|+18** transitions and genuine halt, with complete inactive/parking data and all heads restored. All five handoffs and empty cases are charged. This uses the explicit marked-stream input convention; marker installation/removal has its own actual two-step proofs.

The reusable `wrapper_correct` accepts an actual child Runs/Halts contract on literal entry/return banks, including changing-length output z, and proves exact caller cost **2|x|+2|z|+5|y|+16+t**. The closed bit-flip instance discharges that child premise concretely. Actual-prefix invariants and finite FootprintedRuns prove that push/pop preserve the entire old parking prefix and stay above their markers; copy/flip have corresponding selected/spectator footprint bounds.

`OutputNormalization.compiled_fixedWidth` implements a finite two-stack TM2 converter: the actual MSB-first list `(fixedBits w n).reverse`, with n<2^w, produces canonical `Nat.bits` followed by the existing output suffix, empties the source and genuinely halts. Its exact source cost is w+1 including EOF, with physical bound **10(w+1)**. Pure binary proofs are narrowed from our formalized Problem1.8 solution. No personal Lean library is imported. This is lightweight toolkit interoperability; platypii already has charged normalization. An upstream origin-anchored buffer adapter and any input reversal remain separate programs to implement and charge.

The complete package contains 23 Mathlib/Lean/bundled-only proof modules, retaining the finite compiler, heterogeneous alphabets, exact relative/absolute simulation, same-cost dirty-frame replay, locality, scheduler and asymptotic transport infrastructure. PR64 parking primitives and PR1379 caller tables are explicitly credited under Apache-2.0; no platypii source is copied. The final frontier review covers 1087 recent PR title/body scopes through #1662 at 2026-10-14T05:41Z, with relevant machine sources separately inspected. This is bounded overlap evidence, not a novelty guarantee.

Validation: fresh Lean 4.34.1 rebuild against pinned Mathlib d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612; **1360 defining-module declarations, 788 theorem declarations**, including private/global/generated helpers; zero package axioms and only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound dependencies. Real Lean controls check ownership coverage and reject unused private axioms, public axioms and unproved private theorems. 11 report corruptions and 4 source corruptions are rejected. Supporting literal-table fixtures cover 2704 parking cases and 1785 output-converter cases, with two corrupted-table controls, including optimized Python. Final upload receipt binds the exact staged package; finite fixtures are not universal proof evidence.

Offline source replay: `python3 -I -B research/multitape-proof-toolkit/verify.py`. Dedicated fresh Lean replay: run `replay.py --out /absolute/new/output --cache-project /pinned/cache --lean /path/to/lean` from the package. README/API/PROOF document exact interfaces, VALIDATION.json records checks, and MANIFEST.json binds every shipped file. Generic VERIFY.json runs Python only; the optional formal CI recipe is supplied inside the package. Hosted CI, independent human review and the complete fast multiplication theorem are not claimed.

This provides reusable proved physical building blocks for contributors' verified arithmetic children and recursive routing. It does not submit a new kappa or a completed recursive multiplier. Prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including three parallel agents; source credits and modifications are in NOTICE.md, REUSE.json and PORTING.json.
